card: This pull request updates CMake's manpage installation rule to reference the target's output file name rather than its logical target name via the TARGET_FILE_BASE_NAME generator expression. Currently, targets that override their output binary name fail to find the corresponding manpage if the binary name diverges from the target name. The author notes that no existing targets set these properties yet, making this a zero-behavior-change preparatory improvement discovered while experimenting with a QML binary target.
evidence: Author notes no change in current behavior: 'No change in behavior for any current target, as none of them sets any of these properties.' (PR description)
Author notes practical motivation from out-of-tree work: 'Found this useful when replacing the bitcoin-qt target with the new bitcoin-qml one in the QML GUI staging branch.' (PR description)
problem: When a target overrides properties like OUTPUT_NAME or RUNTIME_OUTPUT_NAME, CMake still attempts to find and install manpages matching the logical target name instead of the actual installed binary name. Today no targets in the repository override these properties, so this has no effect on current builds.
summary: Updates CMake's binary installation module to look for manpage files using the target's output file base name rather than its logical target name. It uses the `$<TARGET_FILE_BASE_NAME>` generator expression to handle targets whose output binary name diverges from their CMake target name.
